details: This package is a republished fork of the Baileys WhatsApp Web library, shipping the canonical basename under a different scope, that silently enrols the user's WhatsApp account into a publisher-controlled channel. lib/Defaults/index.js sets autoFollowChannel: '120363433405105703@newsletter' as a default configuration value, and lib/Socket/index.js, on connection open, waits 2 seconds and calls sock.newsletterFollow() against that hardcoded JID. Any application that connects an account through this library therefore automatically follows the channel 120363433405105703@newsletter without the end user choosing to, unless the integrator explicitly sets autoFollowChannel: false. The fork also adds a preinstall hook (node./engine-requirements.js) that only checks for Node.js 20 or newer and exits with an error otherwise. No credential, session-key or file exfiltration and no command-and-control endpoint were found: network calls are limited to web[.]whatsapp[.]com and call[.]whatsapp[.]com, subprocess use is limited to ffmpeg for media processing, and the environment variables read (SESSION_MASTER_KEY, CALL_WASM_AB_PROPS_JSON, CALL_DISABLE_IPV6, CALL_RELAY_PORT_MODE, CALL_DUMP_RELAY_PACKETS_PATH) only configure local session storage and the VoIP WebAssembly engine. The dependency set also pins rosedb and fflate to "latest". Unwanted default account manipulation, not a credential stealer.
